title: webmcp.utlovat.se — Non-Partisan Election Fact-Checking
pitch: An agent-native election evidence layer where WebMCP exposes published sources, visible gaps, and human-in-the-loop verification directly in the browser. Just in time for the Swedish election 2026.
about_excerpt: An agent-native election evidence layer where WebMCP exposes published sources, visible gaps, and human-in-the-loop verification directly in the browser. Just in time for the Swedish election 2026. Like Comment Story Updates Utlovat.se WebMCP landing page explaining that agents can sort Swedish election evidence but cannot recommend a political party. tlovat.se research brief for healthcare, showing a recorded unclear position for Moderates, 12 evidence records for Social Democrats, Evidence cards in an Utlovat.se research brief, each with a Swedish quote, publication date, four-year cost range, source link, archive copy Inspiration During democratic elections, voters are inundated with conflicting claims, manifesto promises, and shifting party positions. When citizens in general, and first time voters in particular, turn to AI assistants for guidance, your average, I have and answer for everything, general-purpose LLMs present a dangerous hazard: they risk hallucinating plausible quotes, confusing past election cycles with current platforms, and inventing policy stances where parties are actually silent . In high-stakes civic decision-making, an AI summary is not enough. Citizens need evidence, not a verdict. And to be encouraged to question the feasibility of the "five minutes to Election Day" promises. utlovat.se (meaning "As Promised" in Swedish) is aims to be an independent, non-partisan election platform tracking over 2,000 promises and 700+ reviewed parliamentary actions for the 2026 general election. We (actually there is only me and my assisting agents) were inspired to build on OpenAI's WebMCP because it offers the missing piece of the agentic web: a standardized, browser-native protocol that allows a website to expose its immutable, verified evidence directly to AI agents . A perfect fit with how youths of today consume information. What It Does With WebMCP utlovat.se transforms from a static website into an active, agent-native truth layer. Through WebMCP, an AI assistant using a WebMCP-enabled browser gains access to 7 specialized tools in total (5 global + 2 contextual): Grounded Deterministic Search (search_verified_evidence): Queries exact manifesto commitments, returning verified quotes, publication dates, transparent cost approximations (≈), and linked Wayback Machine archive copies when available (we have set a 100% archive target and are very close to achieving it). Interactive Evidence Boards (build_research_brief): Generates side-by-side comparative cards on /granska and /webmcp without recommending any party. (Absolute neutrality in all aspects are paramount) Human-in-the-Loop Protocol Verification (get_evidence_board_status): Ensures that evidence remains strictly unverified until a human visually inspects the primary citations and marks the board as confirmed. Parliamentary Trail Tracing (trace_promise): Connects a 2026 election promise to Handlingsvågen's (our Swedish feature name) database of reviewed Swedish Parliament (Riksdagen) voting records and motion histories. Multi-Party Fiscal Matrix (show_party_comparison): Opens the interactive comparison matrix on /jamfor, accounting for joint coalition proposals without double-counting costs. Contextual On-Page Tools (trace_current_promise, build_current_question_brief): Dynamically activates contextual tools when browsing individual promise pages or topic questions. Honest Silence & Gap Transparency: Explicitly reports when a party has no recorded stance on a query, rather than treating a bounded empty result as proof of a position. How We Built It We built the WebMCP integration natively into utlovat.se using TypeScript, Astro, and Tailwind CSS: WebMCP Client-Side Tool Registry (site/src/scripts/webmcp.ts): We registered our 7 tools directly onto document.modelContext.registerTool, defining JSON schemas with strict parameter typing and non-partisan output structures. Cryptographic Data Hashing: Every tool response includes an authoritative data_hash (SHA-256), anchoring conclusions to a fixed, verifiable dataset snapshot. Web Archive Links: When available, a political quote includes a linked Wayback Machine archive copy, making the source trail inspectable and more resilient to link rot. (And also makes it possible to highlight a change in stance in any question). Parliamentary Open Data Bridge: We engineered client-side JSON API endpoints (/api/v1/promise-traces.json) linking election promises to Swedish Parliament document IDs (e.g. data.riksdagen.se/dokument/HB023145) and chamber voting roll calls. Dedicated English Surface (/webmcp): Built a dedicated English hub with the 5 global WebMCP tools, clear testing prompts and cost-range badges. The 2 contextual tools become available after navigation to an individual promise or topic page. Challenges We Faced Enforcing Strict Epistemic Neutrality: The primary challenge in election technology is preventing algorithmic bias. We designed tool descriptions and read-only output structures that explicitly instruct agents not to declare "kept/broken" verdicts, rank parties, or make subjective recommendations. Honest Silence Reporting: In standard RAG pipelines, an empty search return is ambiguous. We had to architect bounded search semantics so that if a party has no promise on a topic, the agent explicitly returns a structured gap report rather than extrapolating. Sometimes silence speaks a thousand words. Zero-Self-Certification for Human-in-the-Loop: We had to ensure agents could not fake human verification. The get_evidence_board_status tool queries the live DOM state, which only transitions to confirmed ✓ when the physical user clicks the inspection button. Anti-Double-Counting in Coalition Manifestos: Calculating joint party proposals required shared commitment keying so coalition proposals are not counted twice in fiscal matrix calculations. New Additions Developed Exclusively During the Hackathon (from August 25, 2026): 1. Prior Work (Before August 25, 2026): The core Swedish public-information website, Utlovat.se. Its foundational dataset of Swedish election commitments and public evidence, including data/promises.json and Handlingsvågen. Existing non-partisan calculations and Swedish public-facing comparison templates. 2. New Additions Developed During the Hackathon (August 25 – September 3, 2026): Browser-native WebMCP integration ( site/src/scripts/webmcp.ts ): Seven read-only client-side tools—five global tools and two page-contextual tools—registered through document.modelContext.registerTool . English Challenge Surface ( site/src/pages/webmcp.astro ): An English entry point, “Evidence, not a verdict,” with a testing guide and direct display of cost ranges marked with ≈ , their basis, and the four-year assumption where applicable. Visible Research Brief and Evidence Board ( /granska , site/src/pages/granska.astro ): A shared human–agent research surface that renders published quotes, dates, source links, archive copies where available, recorded unclear positions, and bounded gaps. It creates deep-linkable research briefs without recommending a party. Human review boundary ( get_evidence_board_status ): The agent can read whether the person has marked the visible evidence board as reviewed, but cannot mark it reviewed itself. Unread material remains explicitly unverified. Parliamentary action tracing ( /api/v1/promise-traces.json ): A read-only evidence chain from a published campaign promise to its source, archive copy, and recorded, human-reviewed parliamentary actions where available. The tool does not decide whether a promise was kept or broken. Automated WebMCP verification ( site/scripts/test-webmcp.mts , site/scripts/test-webmcp-retest.mts ): Tests of the published browser client, tool registration, evidence fields, archive filtering, visible uncertainty, neutral boundaries, English topic matching, shared links, and contextual tools. Open-source licensing : Apache-2.0 was added to the root repository during the hackathon. Frozen competition release : A separate public repository, bambapappa/utlovat-webmcp-challenge , preserves the final static competition build independently of the continuing election-information service. Its manifest records the selected source commit, data hash, and output hashes before the competition cutoff. Transparent implementation history : The public Git history records the WebMCP implementation commits from August 26 onward, while the separate snapshot repository records the freeze and release procedure. Accomplishments That We're Proud Of Hackathon premiere: This marks the moment of my first ever participation in a Hackathon. Evidence-Bounded Civic Fact-Checking: WebMCP keeps tool outputs tied to published quotes, source URLs, archive copies when available, and a verifiable data hash.
